ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Preventive Visit — Mahalia Jackson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Jackson, 52, comes for her yearly preventive visit six weeks after the review at which the repeat FDG-PET showed no active heart inflammation. Prednisone was reduced to 7.5 mg two weeks ago as planned; she takes methotrexate 20 mg weekly with folic acid, metoprolol, alendronate and vitamin D. She has more energy, climbs two flights of stairs without stopping, and has sung two concerts a week since the spring, with a longer tour planned for later in the autumn. The hoarseness in June settled within ten days. Her defibrillator has given no shocks, and the remote check last month was normal. She sleeps well now that the prednisone dose is lower. Her PHQ-9 today is 3. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1964-10-05; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 92.2 kg, BMI 31.9; blood pressure 128/80 (average of two)
No redness; pupils equal and reactive
Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat
Examined with her agreement and a chaperone: no mass, skin change or nipple discharge; no axillary nodes
Regular rhythm; no murmur; defibrillator pocket healed; no ankle swelling
Old lower midline scar; soft; no liver or spleen enlargement
Speculum examination with her agreement and a chaperone: vaginal cuff healed, no cervix present
No rash, nodules or plaques; no suspicious lesions
Height 170 cm, unchanged; no spinal tenderness

Breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough for three months, worse on tour, with tiredness and chest tightness; she can no longer hold long phrases; bilateral hilar lymph node enlargement on today's chest radiograph; granulomas were reported at an abdominal operation twelve years ago, with no pathology report available: sarcoidosis must be confirmed by tissue and other causes excluded
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented breathlessness during performances and the 1952 granulomas. Superseded by the tissue diagnosis at the consultation.

Palpitations with two spells of light-headedness while singing; ECG today: sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR 240 ms) and frequent ventricular ectopic beats: cardiac involvement must be looked for
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when cardiac sarcoidosis was diagnosed.
Hypercalcemia: calcium 10.8 mg/dL with a high 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D and a low 25-hydroxyvitamin D, while taking an over-the-counter calcium and vitamin D supplement; creatinine slightly raised
S — Synthetic finding; resolved on treatment.

Pulmonary sarcoidosis with hilar and mediastinal lymph node involvement (Scadding stage II), confirmed by non-necrotizing granulomas on EBUS-guided lymph node aspiration with negative stains and cultures; mild restriction and reduced diffusing capacity; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented sarcoidosis
S — Synthetic histology, stage and lung function; her biographer reports a diagnosis of sarcoidosis after granulomas were found at an operation (D, probable).

Acute viral laryngitis: three days of hoarseness, a sore throat and a mild dry cough after a cold, without fever, on prednisone 20 mg and methotrexate; rapid influenza and COVID-19 tests negative; no thrush; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.

Cardiac sarcoidosis: first-degree atrioventricular block, ventricular ectopy (6 percent of beats) with nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, left ventricular ejection fraction 47 percent, patchy late gadolinium enhancement of the basal septum and inferolateral wall, and matching focal FDG uptake on PET; synthetic modern detail linked to the documented private account that sarcoidosis was in her heart
S — Synthetic cardiac findings; the account that her doctors told her sarcoidosis was in her heart rests on her biographer (D, probable), and the interpretation of her later heart disease is R.
Long-term systemic glucocorticoid treatment for sarcoidosis, with bone, glucose, blood pressure, infection and eye risks to manage
Dual-chamber implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, placed after sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia was induced at electrophysiology study; remote monitoring
S — Synthetic device status after the synthetic implant.

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated for a woman of 52 on long-term glucocorticoids and methotrexate. Total cholesterol 204, HDL 54, LDL 126 mg/dL, triglycerides 118; her ten-year cardiovascular risk is about 4 percent, so a statin is not recommended now, with lifestyle advice and a recheck in a year. A1c 6.2% in August is in the prediabetes range, partly from prednisone; a diabetes prevention program was offered. Mammography is due. Colonoscopy six years ago was normal. Cervical screening is not needed: the examination today shows no cervix after her hysterectomy, and she has no history of cervical precancer. Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines given today; her pneumococcal, zoster and hepatitis B series are complete; no live vaccines on her current treatment. [S]
Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines given today.
Screening mammogram ordered.
Diabetes prevention program referral.
Lipids and A1c again in one year, or sooner if prednisone is increased.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Cardiac sarcoidosis in remission on treatment, with a defibrillator (D86.85). No palpitations or shocks; regular rhythm; remote device check last month normal. [S]
Continue the prednisone taper as planned by Dr. Asante-Miller and cardiology.
Continue methotrexate 20 mg weekly.
Methotrexate safety blood tests next month.

Long-term systemic glucocorticoids (Z79.52). Bone density in March showed a femoral neck T-score of -1.6 on starting prednisone; on alendronate, with dietary calcium and vitamin D 1000 units, and calcium normal. [S]
Continue alendronate while on prednisone.
Repeat bone density scan two years after the first.
Eye examination with pressure check in March, one year after the first.

Follow-up: Mammogram within the month. Methotrexate blood tests next month. Pulmonology and cardiology as planned. Next preventive visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 30 minutes, with her consent. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and completed a health care power of attorney. She said that her faith guides her, that she wants every treatment that gives her a good chance to live and to sing, and that if she became so ill that she could not recover to know and pray with the people around her, she would want comfort care and her church's prayers rather than machines. The defibrillator was explained: it can be switched off painlessly by the device team if she ever chooses comfort care at the end of life, and she asked that this be discussed with her agent then. To be revisited at each change in her health and at least yearly. [S]
